quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What are highway signs called that show dangerous conditions?

options.text: Regulatory signs
Warning signs
Information signs
Guide signs

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell drivers about dangers ahead. Follow all warning signs to stay safe. Not following a warning sign can cause an accident.

questions.question: It is safe to stop on railroad tracks for a short time while moving with other vehicles.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Only cross railroad tracks if your entire vehicle can fit on the other side.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead
Divided highway ahead
Two-way traffic ahead
Intersection ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic moves in both directions ahead.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Let pedestrians cross first if they are in the intersection.
Speed up as fast as you can.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first if they are in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green light means you may proceed. But first, make sure any pedestrians or traffic in the intersection have cleared.

questions.question: Driving faster helps you avoid losing control on wet roads.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: On wet roads, your tires can slide on the water. This is called hydroplaning and causes you to lose control. Slow down when roads are wet.

questions.question: What should you do if you get stuck in a snowstorm?

options.text: Leave your car and walk to find help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers to stop.
Stay in your car. You are easier to find there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are easier to find there.
questions.explanation: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. Rescue workers can find you more easily if you stay in your vehicle. Walking in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
Only when driving in rural areas.
When driving under bad weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly is illegal if it disrupts normal traffic flow. Police can cite you for driving too slowly.

questions.question: What does a "No stopping" sign mean?

options.text: Long enough to unload packages.
You need to avoid a crash with another vehicle.
You need to let passengers out.
You stop for less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You need to avoid a crash with another vehicle.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash. A police officer can order you to stop.

questions.question: How do you reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night?

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right edge of the road ahead. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. The glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: When you see a steady green arrow on a traffic signal, what can you do?

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn in the direction of the arrow. First, let any traffic and pedestrians in the intersection pass.
Drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow. First, let any traffic and pedestrians in the intersection pass.
questions.explanation: A green arrow allows you to turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane. Always yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: You can pass, even if it is not safe.
Traffic moves in opposite directions.
You cannot pass.
You can pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes that move in the same direction. You can cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Keep the same
Change
Lower

questions.correctAnswerText: Lower
questions.explanation: Slow down when you turn. This helps you control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and be ready for unexpected situations.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move ahead or drop back so they can see you
Drive at the same speed
Stay in their blind spot
Honk your horn to alert them

questions.correctAnswerText: Move ahead or drop back so they can see you
questions.explanation: Never stay in another driver's blind spot. Move ahead or back so the driver can see you.

questions.question: Which of these drugs can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold medicine
All of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal medications such as prescriptions and over-the-counter drugs. It is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug.

questions.question: When should you return to your original lane after passing another vehicle?

options.text: When you feel far enough ahead of the other vehicle
When the other driver signals you to return
When you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror
When you are directly beside the other vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror
questions.explanation: Use your right turn signal before returning to your lane. Return to the right lane when you can see the entire passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What is your blind spot?

options.text: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
The area directly behind your vehicle.
The area you can see in your rearview mirror.
The area you can see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see without turning your head. They exist on the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you must:

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
Slow down without stopping.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: This is a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, then look for pedestrians and traffic before you enter the intersection.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches you, you must immediately:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and sirens approaches, pull to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: What are ways to reduce hydroplaning risk?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep tires at the correct air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when tires slide on water on the road. To reduce this risk, do not speed on wet roads, keep correct tire air pressure, and replace worn tires.

questions.question: Only vehicles with disability plates or placards can park in disability spaces.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Disability parking spaces are only for vehicles that display disability license plates or disability parking placards.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass from either direction. You may only cross these lines to turn left or to pass pedestrians, cyclists, scooter riders, or skateboarders when it is safe.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance gets worse.
You become less alert.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time. It makes it harder to see clearly and judge speed and distance. It reduces your ability to recover from headlight glare. It also makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Side road.
Low clearance.
Merging traffic.
Prepare to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns you that traffic may enter from a side road ahead.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn, but you are not in the correct lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Go to the next intersection and turn there.
Change lanes safely, then back up to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn at the last moment. If you are not in the right lane to turn, drive to the next intersection. Turn from the correct lane there.

questions.question: You can pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: What can you do to help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow down before using the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. Release the gas pedal first to let your vehicle slow down. Then press the brake pedal firmly and steadily. This turns on your brake lights and stops your vehicle smoothly.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic lights are out due to a power outage?

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to come back.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers what you are doing.
Turn on your hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is out, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop. Go through the intersection slowly and carefully when it is your turn.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Be very careful. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn your radio down so you can listen for a train.
Only go when a flagger tells you it is safe.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Be very careful at all railroad crossings. Cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. Listen for trains and follow any flagger's directions.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to stop completely.
Road conditions are unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop. Let other traffic and pedestrians pass. Then go only when it is safe.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you on the left and a bicyclist is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder.
Go between both of them.
Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Do not try to pass the bike and avoid the car at the same time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the bicycle.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking steps to avoid accidents.
Protecting yourself from bad drivers by passing them in traffic.
Driving very close to the car in front of you.
Changing lanes quickly to move through traffic congestion.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking steps to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you spot dangerous situations and act before an accident happens. It helps you avoid crashes with aggressive, reckless, careless, distracted, or impaired drivers or pedestrians.

questions.question: You are driving uphill and approaching a heavy truck from behind. You should know:

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the posted speed limit.
You may not be able to pass the truck safely.
You may not be able to pass the truck legally.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks go slower than the speed limit, especially uphill. Be careful when approaching a truck from behind. On hills where you cannot see ahead clearly, passing another vehicle is illegal.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move to the left lane. You should:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your turn signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see if any vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive the speed limit with caution.
Never drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when roads are wet or icy from rain, snow, or sleet. Poor road conditions require slower speeds than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: When passing a stopped emergency vehicle on the roadside, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Move away from the emergency vehicle's lane or slow down.
Pull off the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Move into the lane closest to the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move away from the emergency vehicle's lane or slow down.
questions.explanation: The Move Over Law protects police officers, emergency workers, tow truck drivers, and utility workers. You must move to another lane away from a stopped emergency vehicle. If you cannot safely change lanes, you must slow down.

questions.question: You can go through a yellow light if:

options.text: An emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
Pedestrians are crossing.
You are turning right.
You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: What must you do if you see this sign above your lane?

options.text: You cannot exit the freeway.
You can continue on the freeway or exit from your current lane.
You can stay in your lane and continue on the freeway.
You must exit if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must exit if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means your lane leads off the freeway. You can move to another lane to continue, but if you stay in this lane, you must exit.

questions.question: What does a good defensive driver do?

options.text: Always drives slowly.
Watches what other drivers do.
Drives at the same speed all the time.
Only drives in areas they know.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver pays attention to other drivers and expects problems. This helps prevent accidents, even when other drivers are not paying attention.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before passing and check for oncoming traffic.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot before passing left.
Wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal 100 feet before passing. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Wait until you see both headlights in your mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn ahead. Slow down.
Work crew ahead.
Side road.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn ahead. Slow down.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs tell drivers about hazards ahead. This sign warns you of a sharp turn coming. You must slow down.
